title: Canonical integral purity comparison cocycles
statement: Fix the finite-field datum $D$, its coefficient datum $C$, a finite coefficient field $E$, and a smooth separated finite-type morphism $f:X\to Y$ of pure relative dimension $r$ between separated finite-type schemes over $D.k$. Use the specified source and exceptional objects, their reduction maps [def-pur-adic-purity-objects], the normalized scalar family [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality], and the finite reduction comparisons [def-pur-finite-reduction-comparisons]. Assume the actual completed-ring projections satisfy $p_n q_{n,m}=p_m$ for $m\le n$. Let $\alpha$ be the derived tensor associator conjugated by reductionBridge, and $c_N$ the canonical support comparison conjugated by reductionBridge and finiteImageIso. For every integral finite-Tor input $K$ and $m\le n$, reduction of its source comparison followed by the finite source comparison and shifted pullback of $\alpha_Y$ equals $\alpha_X$ followed by its source comparison at $m$. The analogous equation holds for its exceptional comparison, and for $N=H_RK$ or $N=G_RK$ the reduction of $c_N$ followed by the finite support comparison and support of $\alpha_X$ equals $\alpha_Y$ followed by $c_N$ at $m$. These are equalities of actual derived morphisms, with exactly the canonical tensor associators defined by the stated projection identity; equal indices are included.

proof.text:
identify the two derived reduction functors by the unique comparison of
left adjoints to composite scalar restriction. The hypothesis is the equality of
actual completed-ring projections, so this comparison is the tensor associator.
The scalar adjunction units identify it with the direct quotient normalization in
purAdicSource_finiteness_reductions. Substitute this into its source square.
For the exceptional square, transpose under compact support and exceptional inverse
image. The coefficient mate preserves the actual counit, so mate pasting identifies
successive reduction with direct reduction. The integral exceptional tower evaluation
has this same normalization, giving the asserted target square. For support, apply
comparison_composition, conjugate by reductionBridge and finiteImageIso, and use
naturality of these isomorphisms. Its finite comparison is exactly the specified
compact-support scalar mate. This proves the support square for every input N,
hence for the two stated inputs. At equal indices the same unit-normalized adjunction
comparison gives the identity quotient equation; no nonempty-scheme assumption enters.
